title: Can I DEMOLISH Drawback Chess?
summary: Drawback Chess vs online humans; goal 5 wins, achieved in 6 games (5-1). G1 (white) Closed Book vs opp Inside the Lines - W; G2 Obsession vs opp Boastful - W; G3 Pack Mentality-type (pieces must move adjacent to other pieces) vs opp Diplomatic Immunity - W; G4 (white) Hopscotch vs opp Bloodthirsty - L; G5 Flatterer vs opp Snipers - W; G6 Leaps and Bounds vs opp Truant - W.
rules: Standard setup and moves; each player is dealt one secret random drawback (card with Easy-Hard difficulty slider); the opponent's drawback is revealed when the game ends ('Your opponent's drawback was ...').
No check/checkmate: kings may move into or stay in attack; capturing the enemy king wins.
Breaking or failing your drawback condition makes you lose (or the move is simply illegal, depending on drawback wording).
Players may chat/rename to bluff or reveal drawbacks.

Drawbacks in this video: Closed Book - you lose if you ever start your turn while there's an open file. Inside the Lines - you can't move onto the rim. Obsession - if you can move to it (a specific target square shown, e.g. a4 / c1), you must. Boastful - you lose if you have fewer pieces than your opponent. (Pack Mentality) - your pieces must move to squares adjacent to other pieces. Diplomatic Immunity - you can't capture a piece that has just moved unless that move was a capture. Hopscotch - you must alternate moving to light and dark squares. Bloodthirsty - after the first three turns, if you go two turns without capturing, you must capture on the third or lose. Flatterer - if your opponent moves a pawn you must move a pawn; if they move a non-pawn you must move a non-pawn. Snipers - (text not read). Leaps and Bounds - you can't move a piece adjacent to where it was. Truant - you can't move the same piece twice in a row.
win_condition: Capture the enemy king. Goal: 5 wins.
